name: Påarp - Mellbystrand

officialSources.name: Hallandsleden: Påarp - Mellbystrand
facts: Official name Påarp - Mellbystrand.
Official distance 13 km.
Difficulty Grön, normalized here as easy.
No official estimated time shown.

Official description passes Halland's largest Iron Age burial field, beach heath by Laxvik, Gullbranna nature reserve, Genevadsån, Tönnersa nature reserve, Snapparp/Lagaoset, the Lagan crossing, Hökafältet nature reserve and the coastal road in Mellbystrand to Strandhotellet and the bus stop.

The public comment visible on the official page from July 2025 describes the section as varied, pleasant, with many swim/fika places, few transport stretches and easy public transport for partial walks.

The official-source lane reported 21 records using a query variant that included Burgers & Dreams at Mellbystrand.

Category counts from the main-thread 20-record query include 5 year-round toilets, 2 seasonal toilets, 2 drinking-water records, 2 rest-place records, 2 public-transport records, 2 beaches, 5 lodging records, 4 food/drink records, 1 grocery and 2 sights.

officialSources.name: Länsstyrelsen Halland: Gullbranna
facts: Gullbranna is a Halmstad nature reserve, 107 ha, protected since 1972 and part of Natura 2000.
Visitor information describes the Genevadsån outlet, Gullbranna trails, picnic/rest places and a dry toilet at the north parking.
Rules include no tenting/overnighting in caravan or camper, no loose dogs, no cycling except roads/marked cycle trail and no motor vehicles or parking outside designated places.

officialSources.name: Länsstyrelsen Halland: Tönnersa
facts: Tönnersa is a Halmstad/Laholm nature reserve, 288 ha, protected since 1980.
Visitor information warns that Lagaoset shifts through the year and that soft sand around the outlet can be hazardous.
Rules include no tenting/overnighting in caravan or camper, no loose dogs, no cycling except roads/marked cycle trail and no motor vehicles or parking outside designated places.

officialSources.name: Länsstyrelsen Halland: Hökafältet
facts: Hökafältet is a Laholm nature reserve, 417 ha including 51 ha water, protected since 1972 and expanded 2009.
Länsstyrelsen reports a vehicle barrier after the middle reserve parking due damage/theft, but pedestrians and cyclists can pass.
The reserve is part of Laholmsbuktens sanddynsreservat and Natura 2000.
Rules include no tenting, no caravan/camper overnighting, no loose dogs, no cycling except marked roads/cycle route and no motor vehicles or parking outside designated places.

officialSources.name: Laholm sea-bathing/beach rules
facts: Bathing season is 1 May-15 September.
During bathing season dogs may be on ordinary beaches only 18:00-08:00 and must be leashed; Kattvägen dog beach is the exception.
Camping/overnighting on beaches with tent, camper or caravan is prohibited; camping is only allowed at campsites.
Horse use on beaches is allowed outside bathing season; local information says horses are not allowed on the beach 1 May-15 September.
Motor traffic on the beach has been prohibited since 2024-05-31.
Hallandstrafiken bus line 225 is described as running along the coast, with stops such as Birger Pers väg, Kolonivägen and Stora Strandvägen.

officialSources.name: Naturvandra.se: Vandra Hallandsleden mellan Gullbranna naturreservat & Mellbystrand
facts: Published after a 2025-08-26 hike; outbound Gullbranna-Mellbystrand followed Hallandsleden, while return/beach parts were partly off-route.
Report confirms orange Hallandsleden markings, Snapparp toilets/tables and nearby services, a narrow Lagan bridge shared with cyclists, Hökafältet paths/cycleway and Mellbystrand approach.
Report warns about strong underwater currents in rough/windy conditions and treats beach/off-route return details as separate from the marked trail.

dogs: Gullbranna, Tönnersa and Hökafältet prohibit loose dogs.

horses: Laholm allows horses on beaches outside bathing season but not in dunes with animals; local information confirms horses are not allowed on the beach 1 May-15 September.
Halmstad prohibits horses on official beaches 1 May-15 September and in dunes year-round.
